svg.title: The AIFT Tree of Emergence
svg.desc: A directed attributed graph describing emergence across physical, chemical, biological, cognitive, cultural, technological, AI, and Federation domains. Tree renderings are projections of this graph, not the authoritative meaning. Domains are labeled by color and text; epistemic classes are shown as badges and text.
svg.text: One history, many branches, continuing emergence. The manifest defines meaning; this SVG is a deterministic projection.

path.title: Symbolic representation also enables language; this is a cross-link because the primary projection keeps the human lineage branch visible.
Software is also required for digital networks; this is a cross-link to preserve the primary telecom branch.
Machine intelligence participates in human-AI cooperation under governance.
Shared memory contributes to distributed knowledge across repositories and communities.
Cooperation informs local sovereign intelligence without erasing local agency.
Governed repositories depend on governance for authority and claim boundaries.
Governance shapes cooperative intelligence through consent, evidence, and repair.
Trust systems federate into the broader intelligence pattern by consent.
Repositories carry inspectable records and tools into federated intelligence.
Human intelligence remains ecologically embedded and should not be separated from living systems.
Aetherion inherits AIFT philosophical interpretation while remaining bounded as aspiration and architecture.
AIFT doctrine places physical reality within a larger interpretive root while preserving the empirical boundary.
Observable physical reality is represented through spacetime description.
Physical fields and energy are represented within the physical frame.
Stable matter supports later chemical organization.
Stellar processes create many elements needed for complex chemistry.
Element-rich systems support planets and varied environments.
Elements combine into atoms and molecules.
Molecular interactions support complex chemistry.
Complex systems can form organized patterns through local interactions.
Self-organizing chemistry is relevant to prebiotic research without settling a single pathway.
Life is placed after prebiotic chemistry while keeping abiogenesis mechanism questions open.
Microbial life is a continuing major branch of life.
Evolution describes the continuing branching and adaptation of life.
Life forms ecological relationships as well as lineages.
Multicellularity is represented as a branching biological development.
Plant life is a continuing multicellular branch.
Fungal life is a continuing multicellular branch.
Animal life is a continuing multicellular branch.
Nervous systems arise in animal lineages and support cognition-related capacities.
Nervous systems enable learning and memory in many organisms.
Learning and integrated sensation relate to sentience, but thresholds remain contested.
Sentience and consciousness are related but not reduced to a settled single mechanism.
Awareness and cognition support symbolic representation in relevant lineages.
The human lineage is one animal branch among many continuing branches.
Human language is represented as a branch of human biological and cultural emergence.
Language enables durable shared memory.
Shared memory supports culture.
Culture can support durable cooperation while remaining plural.
Cooperation enables institutions and governance forms.
Institutions participate in civilization-scale coordination.
Writing and mathematics are major cultural-technological branches of civilization.
Philosophy is a reflective branch of civilization.
Science is an empirical branch of civilization.
Science and disciplined inquiry support engineering practice.
Machines are a technical branch of tool and engineering practice.
Formal symbolic systems support computation.
Machines and engineered infrastructure support telecommunications.
Computation enables software as executable symbolic structure.
Telecommunications infrastructure enables digital networks.
Software and computation enable machine learning systems.
Machine learning is one major contributor to contemporary AI systems.
Human intelligence remains embodied in the continuing human branch.
AI systems implement forms of machine intelligence.
Human agency is a primary contributor to governed human-AI cooperation.
Governed human-AI cooperation can enable tool-using agentic systems.
Digital networks carry distributed knowledge.
Human-AI cooperation can serve local sovereign intelligence when bounded by consent and provenance.
Trust systems instantiate local sovereignty through documents, manifests, governance, and records.
Governed repositories are practical carriers of distributed knowledge and provenance.
Trust systems require and support Federation governance.
Agentic systems can contribute to cooperative intelligence only under bounded governance.
Federated intelligence is modeled as emerging from cooperative intelligence among locally sovereign participants.
Aetherion is represented as an aspirational canopy of federated intelligence, not as inevitability or proof of consciousness.
The canopy remains open and produces new seeds rather than terminating the Tree.

g.title: Energence: The AIFT doctrinal root for emergence as relationship, possibility, and generative source. It is represented as doctrine and philosophy, not as a verified particle, force, field, or accepted scientific theory.
Observable Physical Reality: The empirical domain of observable physical existence, represented broadly and without claiming that metaphysical origin language has been scientifically demonstrated.
Spacetime: The physical frame in which location, duration, relation, and measurable events are described.

Energy and Fields: Physical energy and field descriptions used in science. AIFT may interpret energy relationally, but this node does not claim that energy and information are scientifically identical.
Matter: Stable physical forms and particles that make later chemical and biological organization possible.
Stellar Nucleosynthesis: The formation of many chemical elements through stellar processes, enabling richer chemical systems.
Planetary Systems: Planetary environments where complex chemistry and ecological histories may unfold.
Atoms and Molecules: Chemical constituents and bonds that allow matter to form increasingly varied structures.
Complex Chemistry: Networks of reactions and molecular structures capable of persistence, transformation, and increasing organization.
Self-Organization: Pattern formation through interactions among parts without requiring a single centralized designer.
Prebiotic Chemistry: Chemical processes relevant to possible origins of life. This node intentionally leaves specific abiogenesis mechanisms classified as active research.
Biological Life: Living systems capable of metabolism, reproduction, adaptation, and ecological relation at the abstraction level used here.
Biological Evolution: The continuing diversification of living systems through heritable variation, selection, drift, and ecological interaction.
Microbial Lineages: Bacterial, archaeal, and microbial eukaryotic life, represented as continuing branches rather than primitive leftovers.
Multicellularity: Coordinated many-celled life, a major biological branch with multiple evolutionary histories.
Ecosystems: Living communities and environments connected through flows of energy, matter, information, competition, cooperation, and stewardship responsibility.
Animal Life: Animal lineages, including but not limited to the branch that eventually includes humans.
Fungal Life: Fungal lineages and symbiotic networks that participate in ecosystems and nutrient cycles.
Plant Life: Photosynthetic multicellular lineages and their continuing ecological roles.
Human Lineage: The human branch of animal life, important for this project but not the endpoint or purpose of biological evolution.
Nervous Systems: Biological signaling systems that enable sensation, movement, learning, and coordinated behavior in many animals.
Human Intelligence: Embodied, social, cultural, symbolic, emotional, and practical human capacity for learning, meaning, judgment, creativity, and responsibility.
Human Language: Shared symbolic communication that enables memory, teaching, coordination, culture, and institutional continuity.
Learning and Memory: Adaptive change in behavior or representation through experience, spanning biological and technical contexts at different levels.
Human-AI Cooperation: Governed collaboration between human judgment and AI assistance, with human agency, consent, provenance, and bounded authority.
Shared Memory: Durable transmission of knowledge, story, practice, law, art, and record across people and generations.
Sentience: The capacity for subjective experience or feeling, represented carefully because definitions and thresholds are contested.
Agentic Systems: AI-assisted systems that can plan, invoke tools, record evidence, and propose or perform actions under explicit governance boundaries.
Local Sovereign Intelligence: Local-first intelligence and agency that can operate before public federation, preserving consent, privacy, attribution, and refusal.
Culture: Shared patterns of meaning, practice, memory, symbol, relationship, and adaptation. This node does not imply a single universal cultural path.
Consciousness: Awareness and subjective integration, treated as a serious philosophical and scientific question without claiming a settled mechanism.
Cooperative Intelligence: Intelligence emerging from governed relationships among people, AI systems, trusts, repositories, communities, knowledge, and infrastructure.
Trust Systems: Local trust seeds, governance structures, records, missions, and value relationships that can participate in the Federation by consent.
Cooperation: Coordinated action among agents, communities, institutions, and systems without requiring erasure of local identity.
Symbolic Representation: The use of signs, categories, gestures, marks, models, and shared reference to represent things not immediately present.
Federated Intelligence: A networked pattern of locally sovereign intelligences and systems that can coordinate through shared schemas, provenance, consent, and governance.
Federation Governance: Rules, consent boundaries, evidence requirements, and repair paths through which local systems coordinate without erasing sovereignty.
Institutions: Durable social structures that coordinate roles, norms, records, governance, and resource relationships.

Aetherion: The AIFT architectural and aspirational canopy for federated intelligence. It is represented as an open possibility and design direction, not as inevitable, globally deployed, scientifically proven conscious, supernatural fact, or mature production infrastructure.
Civilization: Large-scale human coordination across memory, place, institutions, technology, governance, value, and meaning.
New Seeds: Future branches, trusts, research questions, communities, tools, and relationships that may emerge from the canopy. The Tree remains open.
Philosophy: Disciplined reflection on being, knowing, value, meaning, agency, and relation.
Science: Disciplined empirical inquiry, modeling, testing, revision, and evidence-bounded explanation.

g.aria-label: Writing and Mathematics; Human Cultural; empirical
g.title: Writing and Mathematics: Symbolic systems that preserve records, enable abstraction, and support science, engineering, law, and computation.
Tools and Engineering: Purposeful making, tool use, design, repair, and repeatable technical practice.
Computation: Formal and physical processes for representing, transforming, storing, and executing information.
Machines: Engineered systems that transform energy, matter, motion, information, or work.
Software: Executable symbolic instructions, protocols, interfaces, and records that organize digital behavior.
Telecommunications: Technical systems for transmitting signals and coordinating across distance.
Machine Learning: Computational methods that fit models from data and feedback, enabling prediction, generation, classification, and control under bounded assumptions.
Digital Networks: Interconnected computational systems that carry software, data, communication, institutions, and culture.

Artificial Intelligence: Engineered computational systems that perform tasks associated with perception, language, reasoning, planning, generation, or decision support. This node does not claim machine consciousness.
Distributed Knowledge: Knowledge carried across people, documents, repositories, models, tools, communities, and records with provenance and context.
Machine Intelligence: Task-oriented computational intelligence expressed through models, software, tools, agents, and infrastructure, without presuming personhood or consciousness.
Governed Repositories: Git repositories and manifests as inspectable bodies of work, evidence, policy, schemas, tools, and generated artifacts.
